 India climb to fourth in WTC standings after Bangladesh slip
 By: Agencies 
 Date:
 November 1, 2026 
 Share post:
 WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin 
 New Delhi, Oct 31: India moved up to fourth place in the World Test Championship (WTC) points table after Bangladesh slipped to fifth following their defeat to the West Indies in the first Test at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium in Dhaka on Saturday.
India, who were previously fifth, now occupy the fourth spot with a points percentage (PCT) of 51.52, while Bangladesh dropped to 47.62 after suffering their third defeat in the ongoing WTC cycle.
Before the result, Bangladesh were ahead of India with a PCT of 55.56, having registered three victories and a draw from six matches. India, meanwhile, had accumulated five wins and two draws from 11 Tests.
The latest change in standings has given India a significant boost in their bid to improve their position in the current WTC cycle, although their PCT remains below that of the leading teams.
Australia continue to occupy the top position in the standings, followed by South Africa and Sri Lanka, while India have moved ahead of Bangladesh into fourth place. The West Indies remain eighth despite their victory, but improved their PCT from 20.83 to 26.92, bringing them closer to seventh-placed Sri Lanka, who have a PCT of 33.33.
The Caribbean side are also targeting a stronger finish in the championship standings, with captain Roston Chase expressing the team’s ambition to break into the top six or five before the conclusion of the current cycle.India will now look to build on their improved position as the competition for places in the WTC final gathers momentum. (IANS)
